name: Microsoft Corporation
monetization: Sells AI via Azure cloud consumption and Copilot seats across Microsoft 365/GitHub/Dynamics; holds ~27% of OpenAI plus a capped 20% revenue share; funds it with ~$190B/yr of capex.
description_md: Microsoft is one of the four US hyperscalers, spanning Azure cloud infrastructure, the Microsoft 365 productivity franchise, Windows, LinkedIn, and gaming. Azure crossed $100B of annual revenue in FY2026 (ended June 30, 2026), making it the anchor of the company's AI story. Microsoft is OpenAI's original backer ($13.8B invested, ~27% of OpenAI Group PBC after the Oct 2025 recapitalization) and simultaneously one of the largest buyers of third-party neocloud capacity (CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Nscale, IREN) to relieve its own capacity constraints.
ai_monetization_md: Three channels: (1) **Azure AI consumption** — Azure surpassed $100B of revenue in FY2026, with AI services a major growth driver; OpenAI itself is a large Azure customer under a $250B contracted commitment made at the Oct 2025 recapitalization. (2) **Copilot seats** — per-seat AI up-sell across Microsoft 365, GitHub, Dynamics and Security. (3) **OpenAI economics** — a 20% revenue share from OpenAI (capped and running through 2030 after the Apr 2026 amendment) plus the ~27% equity stake, carried under the equity method. Microsoft's share of OpenAI's results flows through its P&L, making Microsoft's 10-Q the only public window into OpenAI's profitability: a $3.1B hit in FY26-Q1 implied a ~$11.5B OpenAI quarterly loss, while the nine months to Mar 2026 showed $5.9B of net *gains*, mostly a one-time dilution gain from the recapitalization.
ai_strategy_md: Spend ahead of demand: ~$190B of CY2026 capex guidance (up ~61% y/y; ~$25B of the increase attributed to memory-price inflation, and ~$175B on a comparable basis after a lease-accounting change). Diversify beyond OpenAI following the Apr 2026 amendment that ended exclusivity: Microsoft keeps a non-exclusive IP license through 2032 and first-on-Azure shipping rights, has announced up to $5B of equity in Anthropic (Nov 2025) alongside Anthropic's $30B Azure commitment, and rents massive third-party capacity — Nebius (up to $19.4B), Nscale (~$20–23B, ~200K GB300s), Lambda (multibillion), IREN ($9.7B) — roughly $60B+ across the four per SPEC-tracked contracts. Extended datacenter useful lives from 15 to 25 years effective FY27, shifting future leases from finance to operating treatment.
risk_notes_md: **OpenAI exposure on three axes:** equity (~27%, equity-method losses recur once dilution gains wash out), the $250B Azure commitment (committed, not yet revenue — the largest single line in Azure's backlog), and the capped revenue share. **Commitment quality:** Microsoft's RPO (~$460B per press comparisons, mid-2026) includes large frontier-lab commitments whose funding is not fully identified. **Capex escalation:** the $190B CY26 plan exceeded consensus by ~$35B, with memory inflation a stated driver; depreciation-life extension (15→25 yrs for datacenters) lowers reported expense and is part of the ecosystem-wide useful-life debate (see Insights). **Counterparty web:** Microsoft is simultaneously investor in and customer of Anthropic, and customer of neoclouds (CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Nscale) whose creditworthiness depends on Microsoft's own renewals.

events.title: OpenAI recapitalization: Microsoft takes ~27% of OpenAI Group PBC; OpenAI commits $250B of Azure purchases
events.why_it_matters: Converts Microsoft's $13.8B of capped-profit interests into conventional equity (~$135B implied) and books the largest single cloud commitment on record; Microsoft loses right of first refusal as OpenAI's compute provider.

events.title: Microsoft-OpenAI partnership restructured: revenue share capped through 2030, exclusivity and AGI clause removed
events.why_it_matters: OpenAI's 20% revenue share to Microsoft becomes capped and AGI-independent; Microsoft's IP/model license runs non-exclusively to 2032 with first-on-Azure shipping; OpenAI can sell on any cloud. Changes the quality of both the rev-share stream and the $250B Azure commitment.

events.title: Guides to ~$190B of CY2026 capital spending, ~$35B above consensus
events.why_it_matters: Repriced the whole AI capex complex; management attributed ~$25B of the increase to memory-price inflation rather than added capacity.

events.title: FY2026 results: Azure crosses $100B of annual revenue
events.why_it_matters: The first $100B cloud-infrastructure year for any vendor; validates the revenue side of the capex program and anchors AI-revenue estimates for the whole sector.
